verdict.rationale: Hatchet's architecture clearly separates a central control plane (orchestration, scheduling, coordination) from workers that execute task code, and docs describe self-hosting the control plane as an alternative to (implicitly) Hatchet Cloud managing it — supporting the general BYO-worker/managed-plane model. However, no evidence explicitly confirms that with Hatchet Cloud, workers run entirely in the customer's own network with code/data staying local, nor is there documentation on network isolation, data residency, or security boundaries for this hybrid deployment mode. Missing for 10: explicit vendor statement that Hatchet Cloud's managed control plane never touches worker code/data, documentation of the worker connection protocol (e.g., outbound-only gRPC) for network isolation, and any customer/independent confirmation of this hybrid deployment in production.
